claims.text: Atomic site-occupancy disorder governs superconducting behavior in Nb–Ta–Hf–Zr–Ti refractory high-entropy alloys.
Atomic site-occupancy disorder modulates electron scattering.
Changes in electron scattering affect the formation of coherent Cooper pairs.
As-cast or rapidly quenched Nb–Ta–Hf–Zr–Ti exhibits high atomic disorder.
Rapid quenching preserves a high level of atomic disorder.
Extended sub-solidus annealing reduces atomic site-occupancy disorder.
The proposed annealing treatment can reduce disorder without altering alloy composition.
Enhanced atomic disorder increases electron scattering.
Increased electron scattering disrupts Cooper-pair formation.
Disruption of Cooper-pair formation suppresses the superconducting transition temperature.
Reducing atomic disorder diminishes electron scattering.
Reduced electron scattering promotes Cooper-pair stability and raises the superconducting transition temperature.
The annealed, more ordered sample will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than the quenched, more disordered sample.
The annealed sample will have a sharper superconducting transition than the quenched sample.
The as-quenched baseline is maximally disordered.
The as-quenched baseline has a lower transition temperature and a broader superconducting transition.
Grain boundaries, phase composition, strain, and related microstructural parameters can affect the superconducting transition temperature.
XRD and TEM can establish that atomic site-occupancy disorder is the only significant microstructural difference between the two samples.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only when annealing does not alter other relevant microstructural parameters, whereas the falsification rule treats detection of such additional changes as falsification. Additional changes would instead confound or invalidate the proposed controlled comparison rather than directly falsify the disorder mechanism.
